about: How every kind of part in Data/Parts/parts.json (the Torque Shed catalogue) comes onto a bike. 'slot': it goes in that slot; a part with no authored model there gets a placeholder look (the closest authored part of the slot, or stock, tinted the catalogue colour). 'tune': it changes how the bike goes or sounds, not how it looks (its own slot, no model). 'loose': no authored mount; geometry mode snaps it to the nearest interface it can use ('mounts': socket types, or 'surface:<unit>'), as a box of 'size' metres (forward, up, across; scaled by 'scale_field' against 'scale_at'). 'refuse': it can't be fitted, and why. Read by Fit/Fitment.cpp (BikeFit::AddCatalogue).

engine.refuse: An engine swap needs its own model, mounts and tune: it comes with the engine phase.

frame.refuse: The frame is what everything else fits to: a new frame is a new bike.

fork.refuse: A fork changes the steering geometry the riding physics uses: forks come with the physics step.

shock.refuse: Shocks change the suspension the riding physics uses: they come with the physics step.

wheel.refuse: A wheel changes the radius and weight the riding physics uses: wheels come with the physics step.

disc.refuse: Brakes change how the riding physics stops: they come with the physics step.

caliper.refuse: Brakes change how the riding physics stops: they come with the physics step.

master.refuse: Brakes change how the riding physics stops: they come with the physics step.

swingarm.refuse: A swingarm changes the wheelbase and suspension the riding physics uses: it comes with the physics step.

petrol.refuse: A consumable: you use it on the bike in the shed, you don't fit it.
